title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA donated Agent Substrate, an open-source sandboxed-agent runtime, to the CNCF Sandbox; it multiplexes many idle-heavy agent sessions over a small pool of warm Kubernetes worker Pods via checkpoint/restore, claiming 10x density over standard containers. NVIDIA positions it alongside Dynamo (agent-aware inference routing that feeds GPU signals back to the runtime) and KAI Scheduler within the DSX AI factory stack, explicitly to keep agent infrastructure on open Kubernetes rather than proprietary runtimes.

insights.claim: AI agents spend most of their time idle waiting on prompts, tool results or model responses, so one-Pod-per-session Kubernetes deployments hold memory for inactive sessions while deleting Pods between turns incurs multi-second cold starts and loses agent state.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Agent workloads create demand for a new runtime layer between Kubernetes and agent frameworks; a utilization problem for anyone hosting agents at scale.
insights.quote: AI agents spend most of their time idle, waiting on a human prompt, a tool result or a model response. Kubernetes wasn’t built for that.
insights.locator: AI agents spend most of their time idle

insights.claim: Spinning up a Kubernetes Pod requires traversing the API server, admission, etcd, scheduler, kubelet, image pulls and network setup, taking seconds — far too slow for agent sandboxes that must run 10 ms bash commands hundreds of times per second.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Pod-level orchestration latency is a structural bottleneck for agentic compute; sandbox-runtime vendors that bypass it have a real wedge.

insights.claim: Platform teams running agents on plain Kubernetes face a binary trade-off: keep a warm Pod per agent and pay for mostly-idle compute, or create Pods on demand and pay a cold-start penalty on every step.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Frames the cost economics of agent hosting: idle-compute waste vs latency — whoever collapses this trade-off captures agent-platform spend.

insights.claim: Agent Substrate, donated by NVIDIA to the CNCF Sandbox, is an open-source zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents claimed to run millions of agents and tools at 10x higher density than standard containers.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: A 10x density claim directly lowers CPU/memory cost per agent session; watch adoption by agent-platform and coding-assistant providers.
insights.quote: engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers
insights.locator: Agent Substrate, now donated to the

insights.claim: Agent Substrate runs a separate control plane that maps many actors onto a small pool of ready Kubernetes worker Pods, snapshotting idle actors (memory and filesystem) out of gVisor or microVM sandboxes and restoring them onto any free worker without a trip through the API server, scheduler or kubelet.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Checkpoint/restore multiplexing is the core technical mechanism enabling agent density; similar to serverless snapshotting applied to stateful agents.
insights.locator: Agent Substrate uses Kubernetes for running

insights.claim: NVIDIA frames its upstream contribution to Agent Substrate as a counter to agentic infrastructure fragmenting into proprietary runtimes that bypass Kubernetes.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is commoditizing the agent-sandbox layer via open source, pressuring proprietary sandbox/runtime startups while pulling agent workloads toward its GPU-centric stack.
insights.quote: As agentic infrastructure fragments into proprietary runtimes that bypass Kubernetes, NVIDIA is contributing upstream to keep this work open.
insights.locator: Agent Substrate, now donated to the

insights.claim: Agent Substrate remains immature: its APIs are still changing, GPU support is being rebuilt on Kubernetes DRA, and parts of the Dynamo integration are experimental.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Production adoption is early; treat density claims as forward-looking until GA.

themes.theme: Demand drivers: coding agents, RL, GPU sandboxes

insights.claim: Coding-assistant platforms serving thousands of sessions cannot afford a dedicated warm sandbox per user, yet users expect environments to persist between turns and respond immediately.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Coding-agent providers face sandbox cost scaling with users; density tooling is margin-relevant for them.

insights.claim: RL post-training with verifiable rewards can grow from a few hundred sandboxes in early experiments to many hundreds of thousands in production, and the slowest environment gates the trainer's next batch so sandbox cold starts leave GPUs idle.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: RL environments are becoming a large CPU-sandbox workload adjacent to GPU training; CPU-side latency directly hits expensive GPU utilization.
insights.quote: The slowest environment determines when the trainer gets its next batch, so cold starts on that path leave GPUs idle.

insights.claim: Research coding agents increasingly need short-lived, isolated GPU sandboxes to compile CUDA, benchmark kernels or run numerical jobs, requiring fast start and fair sharing of a limited GPU pool.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: A new GPU consumption pattern — agent-driven, bursty, short-lived — favors fractional/shared GPU scheduling.

insights.claim: Agent Substrate added request parking (#221) so that when all workers are busy, incoming turns are held with a bounded wait and capped queue instead of failing, plus per-container CPU/memory limits for microVM sandboxes (#859) so a runaway helper container is stopped without killing the agent.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Signals the runtime is designed for oversubscription — the economic basis of its density claim.
insights.locator: Request parking in the Agent Substrate router

insights.claim: GPU checkpoints can usually be restored only onto the same GPU model and sometimes only the same driver version, so Agent Substrate proposes a vendor-neutral DRA-based design that records device properties per snapshot and restores onto a matching device or falls back to a cold start; NVIDIA GPUs are the first target.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: GPU state portability is a hard constraint on suspending GPU sandboxes; hardware-homogeneous fleets benefit, mixed fleets face cold-start fallback.
insights.quote: A GPU checkpoint can usually be restored only onto the same GPU model, and sometimes only with the same driver version.

insights.claim: NVIDIA Dynamo's router combines KV-cache location and GPU load with agent signals (session identity, priority, expected output length, tool-call boundaries) to keep related calls on cache-holding workers, prioritize interactive turns, preserve prompts across tool-call gaps and evict cache from terminated subagents first.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Agent-aware KV-cache routing reduces repeated prefill GPU cost for agent loops — a differentiator for NVIDIA's inference software stack.

insights.claim: Dynamo feeds inference signals such as projected time to first token, completion time, cache readiness and GPU-pool saturation back to Agent Substrate so it can suspend agents during long inference waits and resume them as responses near completion — described as the most important part of the integration.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Cross-layer CPU/GPU co-scheduling tightens NVIDIA's software lock-in: the runtime works best when paired with NVIDIA's inference stack.
insights.quote: The most important part of the integration is that Dynamo exposes inference signals to Agent Substrate
insights.locator: The most important part of the integration

insights.claim: At fleet scale, Dynamo feedback can tune warm-worker capacity, regulate agent and subagent fan-out, and avoid activating CPU sandboxes that would sit idle behind a saturated GPU queue.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: Suggests future agent platforms will throttle CPU-side agent activity based on GPU queue state — GPU remains the binding constraint.
insights.locator: At fleet scale, the same feedback

insights.claim: In NVIDIA's DSX AI factory stack, Dynamo, KAI Scheduler and the Kubernetes foundation (AI Cluster Runtime, GPU Operator, Network Operator) are DSX OS components, while Agent Substrate is an independent CNCF project that integrates with them and KAI Scheduler places Substrate worker Pods alongside GPU trainers and inference servers.
insights.speaker: Ekin Karabulut
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is building a full-stack 'AI factory' software layer from scheduling to agents, broadening its moat beyond silicon.
